effort: Prepare the next plant early while linking two planned changes of direction.
brief: E2 is a two-corner Z route. A short W introduces alternating plants, a triangle changes gait between corners, a U route sustains a rounded return, diagonal bounds link forward-moving landings, and a grounded rotational release supplies force transfer without another cut.
marker: In E2, record whether braking begins before both corners and whether the second exit remains controlled; score each corner separately rather than treating a fast total time as success.
readiness: Only link corners when each incoming leg can be slowed under control. With unknown prior response, keep the short routes at moderate entry intent and do not race the second corner. Each attempt is the complete stated route.
space: Use a measured 9 m × 6 m bay with one active route. All short legs, rounded returns and final 2 m stopping corridors fit its declared length; width and escape clearance require measurement. Ball work uses a cleared floor-impact lane and an appropriate low-bounce ball.

drills.name: W Drill Forward Cuts — short three-leg route
drills.execution: Run three 1 m diagonal legs that continue generally forward, changing between left and right diagonals at two cones; stop over 2 m after the last leg.
drills.job: Look and prepare for the second plant before arriving at it.
drills.layout: Mark a forward zigzag with 1 m legs and a clear final stopping line. Both left and right plant directions occur once in the route; no cone touching.
drills.difference: Two linked alternating cuts in one forward course rather than one isolated cut.
drills.regress: Lower speed on all three legs if the second plant becomes late; do not add routes to compensate.
drills.exposure: 2 discrete cuts and 3 braking episodes; both plant directions included.

drills.name: Z Route — Two Square Corners
drills.execution: Run 1.5 m, cut 90 degrees for 1 m, then cut 90 degrees the opposite way and run 1.5 m; stop over 2 m.
drills.job: Main two-corner practice: retain a useful body position for the second plant after the first exit.
drills.layout: Three legs form a Z-like offset route with parallel first/last legs. Mark each corner and reserve the last 3.5 m exit/stop; mirror one route at a time.
drills.difference: Two opposing square cuts joined by a short lateral leg; no previous isolated corner or continuous curve has this route/contact structure.
drills.regress: Lower the middle-leg speed if the second corner is rushed or the plant foot reaches too wide.
drills.exposure: 2 cuts and 3 braking episodes per route.

drills.name: Triangle Shuffle-Sprint Drill
drills.execution: On an equilateral triangle with 1.5 m sides, run the first leg, shuffle the second while facing the centre, then open and run the third; stop over 2 m beyond the start on the final heading.
drills.job: Change gait while preparing two differently oriented plants.
drills.layout: Each route travels 4.5 m before the 2 m stop. Only the two intermediate vertices are cuts; the start/finish is a terminal stop, not a third turn. Clear the outgoing stop line beyond the start.
drills.difference: Two running/shuffle transitions around a closed triangle, unlike the all-running W or Z routes.
drills.regress: Reduce travel speed if the facing change causes crossed feet at a vertex.
drills.exposure: 2 cuts and 3 braking episodes per route; no added start-line turn.

drills.name: U-Drill Turn-and-Go
drills.execution: Run 1.5 m, follow a semicircle of radius 0.5 m and run 1.5 m back on the parallel leg; stop over 2 m. Keep the arc controlled rather than making one hard pivot.
drills.job: Sustain force around a rounded return when a discrete 180-degree plant is unnecessary.
drills.layout: Semicircle length about 1.57 m; total path 4.57 m plus 2 m stop. The parallel lanes are 1 m apart inside the cleared bay, not separate occupied facility lanes.
drills.difference: Rounded half-loop joining parallel legs instead of the original planted same-line shuttle reversal.
drills.regress: Lower speed around the tight arc if the athlete crosses feet or pivots abruptly.
drills.exposure: Continuous 180-degree heading change; 0 discrete cuts and 1 terminal braking episode counted.

drills.name: Forward Zigzag Bounds — two flights
drills.execution: Bound forward-left to the opposite leg, then forward-right to the original leg, or mirror; hold the second landing 2 s. Each flight no more than 0.4 m.
drills.job: Redirect lateral force while continuing to gain forward position between plants.
drills.layout: Two small diagonal landing targets in a 3 m × 3 m clear area; no extra approach steps or third bound.
drills.difference: Both flights retain forward travel with alternating diagonal vectors; earlier pairs returned laterally or switched from diagonal to pure lateral.
drills.regress: Shorten both flights if the first landing cannot support the second push.
drills.exposure: 2 unilateral landings, one each leg, per route.

drills.name: Split-Stance Rotational Scoop Slam
drills.execution: Hold a light slam ball near the rear hip in a split stance. Drive through the legs and rotate hips/trunk together to release low into the floor 1 m diagonally forward; allow the rear foot to unload and reorient.
drills.job: Transfer force through a changing torso direction without adding a running plant or jump.
drills.layout: Use a low-bounce ball and clear all impact/retrieval space. If unsuitable, use instead a stationary split-stance band rotational punch with a light band loop held by the rear hand close to the hip, 1 × 2 per side; remove two throws and log four grounded resisted efforts.
drills.difference: Rotation from a fixed split base, unlike Class 2's translating lateral weight-shift projection.
drills.regress: Reduce load and rotation if the knee stays fixed while the trunk twists or the arms dominate.

light.job: Control knee/pelvis alignment before repeated plants.
Maintain foot-edge control as the travel direction alternates.

strength.job: Shared knee/hip braking capacity without another high-balance task after linked cuts.
Retain hip-hinge strength for repeated exits.
Frontal acceptance for the alternating corners.
Knee-flexor support with a small isometric dose.
Adductor support through successive side changes.
Bent-knee ankle force for low positions at both corners.

previous_review: Class 8 prescribed four discrete cuts, eight unilateral flight landings and ten primary bouts. Actual completion, symptoms and recovery remain unknown.
progression: Introduce linked corners by cutting route lengths and repetitions; the main Z receives two complete routes, four corner practices. Total discrete cuts rise to ten while unilateral landings and strength bouts fall; this is a conditional redistribution, not proof of readiness.
strength_progression: Use one round per lift and a stable goblet squat instead of the supported single-leg hinge emphasis. RDL, lateral lunge, bridge, Copenhagen and soleus keep familiar execution/reserve. Calibrate the goblet load; do not raise other loads with the new route demand.
audit: Removed long standard cone-test distances. Counted only intermediate triangle vertices as cuts, distinguished the rounded U from a planted shuttle and limited bounds to four landings. No best-time racing or exhaustive multi-cone intervals.
next: Next class applies planned gait changes on compact routes; review the actual number and quality of second plants before delivery.

light_entries.name: Lateral Step-Down — low support, light
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight first; a light dumbbell only if still easy. Lower **3 s**, lightly touch the free heel, return under control. Rest **30 s between legs; 45 s before S2**.
light_entries.regress: Rehearse the plant leg controlling knee travel and pelvic position during weight acceptance. Use the lowest stable support that permits a level pelvis and whole stance-foot contact; use hand support if needed. Reduce step height/load for knee collapse or pelvic drop.
light_entries.alternative: If the step is unsuitable, use instead a hand-supported shallow single-leg squat, the same 1 × 4 per leg and easy effort.
light_entries.job: Control knee/pelvis alignment before repeated plants.

light_entries.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
light_entries.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
light_entries.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
light_entries.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
light_entries.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.
light_entries.job: Maintain foot-edge control as the travel direction alternates.

strength_entries.name: Goblet Squat
strength_entries.execution: Dumbbell held close; lower 3 s through owned range and stand decisively with both feet grounded.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/depth if the trunk folds or heels lift.
strength_entries.job: Shared knee/hip braking capacity without another high-balance task after linked cuts.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Retain hip-hinge strength for repeated exits.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Frontal acceptance for the alternating corners.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Knee-flexor support with a small isometric dose.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Adductor support through successive side changes.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Bent-knee ankle force for low positions at both corners.
